scope.evidence_basis: Actual author reconstruction: On a radius-R circle the mode cos(theta) has eigenvalue R^-2, below 1 when R>1; m=1 is a genuine failure of the unrestricted normalized statement. A boundary introduces an unaccounted boundary term; this is proof noncoverage, not a claim that all boundary eigenvalue estimates are false. Dropping the Hessian leaves only m-1, which explains retaining its trace.
